newsitem.title: ITALY: Prodi and Chirac begin substantive summit talks.
newsitem.headline: Prodi and Chirac begin substantive summit talks.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi and President Jacques Chirac of France met on Friday for bilateral summit talks following strains over economic and monetary union and the value of the lira.
The two men shook hands and smiled warmly when Prodi greeted Chirac at the entrance to the 17th century Royal Palace in the southern port city of Naples where the talks were taking place.

They were expected to hold almost two hours of face-to-face discussions before a one-hour plenary session with financial, foreign and other key ministers. A news conference was scheduled for around 1030 GMT.

The morning summit, following a state dinner on Thursday night, was being held in the shadow of a bitter clash earlier this week over whether Italy would make the grade for founding membership of Europe's planned single currency in 1999.
Chirac publicly cast doubt on Italy's fitness to do so on Tuesday and has also repeated criticism this week of the impact of a devalued lira on French exports.
Both men have smoothed over the issue since Chirac rowed back following a threat from an angry Prodi to scrap the brief summit. Neither made any comment to reporters on Friday.

The lira and Italian bonds have soared in recent days after Prodi drew up a tough 62.5 trillion lire ($41 billion) budget for 1997 which he says will cut Italy's deficit sufficiently for it to join monetary and economic union.
"The markets began to react when they saw that this is an important budget," Italian Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi told reporters in Naples.
He presented the measures to parliament on Thursday.

The lira left Europe's exchange rate mechanism (ERM) four years ago in a currency crisis and lost around 40 percent of its value but has since regained some 20 percent and stood on Friday at 992.85 to the German mark, close to its August 1994 level.
Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini told Reuters Financial Television in Naples that he expected the lira to return to the ERM soon.
